title: The Future Of Co2 Emissions In Sprawled Urban Areas
abstract: Is the pace of technological progress sufficient to deliver a carbon-neutral urban transport system by 2050? To what extent could tax-based policies complement technological progress, and at what social cost? We use a new urban environmental general equilibrium model to evaluate baseline and counterfactual scenarios for the evolution of urban transport CO2 emissions. We simulate the evolution of travel demand, modal split and commuting distance upon the spatial configuration of Auckland, New Zealand, which we use an example of a sprawled urban area. We demonstrate that technological progress will have eliminated only 45% of these emissions by 2050. Taxing carbon and urban congestion could further remove 35% of current CO2 emissions. We argue that carbon and congestion taxes should continuously grow to offset the exacerbating environmental burden and the rebound effects technological progress generates. We also compute the associated welfare costs and highlight the resulting policy trade-off between achieving carbon neutrality and economic efficiency. We outline policies to mitigate that trade-off and discuss ways to secure a societally inclusive and economically efficient transition to carbon neutrality.
abstract_zh: 技术进步的速度是否足以在2050年之前实现城市交通的碳中和？税收政策能在多大程度上补充技术进步，且社会成本又是多少？我们使用一个新的城市环境一般均衡模型，评估城市交通二氧化碳排放演变的基准情景和反事实情景。我们以新西兰奥克兰为例（我们将其作为蔓延型城市的范例），根据其空间格局模拟出行需求、交通方式结构和通勤距离的演变。我们表明，到2050年，技术进步只能消除这些排放中的45%。对碳排放和城市拥堵征税，可以进一步消除当前二氧化碳排放的35%。我们认为，碳税和拥堵税应当持续增长，以抵消技术进步所产生的不断加剧的环境负担和反弹效应。我们还计算了相关的福利成本，并强调了实现碳中和与经济效率之间由此产生的政策权衡。我们概述了缓解这一权衡的政策，并讨论了如何确保向碳中和实现包容性且经济高效的转型。

Energy taxes and economic growth in OECD countries: a simultaneous equations approach
venue: Journal of Environmental Economics and Policy
abstract: This paper explores the channels through which energy taxes may affect economic growth, using a simultaneous equations model for a balanced panel data of 31 OECD countries over the 1994–2013 period. The empirical results reveal a negative impact of energy taxes on physical investment in the short and long term. This impact is negatively sensitive to the existence and level of public debt. Additionally, the results show that energy taxes have an indirect effect on human capital through their impact on polluting emissions. The taxes on energy products are able to reduce both the flux and the stock of polluting emissions that have a negative impact on human capital skills in the short and long term. Finally, we found that energy taxes could encourage eco-innovation in the short and long term.
abstract_zh: 本文利用1994至2013年间31个经合组织国家平衡面板数据的联立方程模型，探讨了能源税影响经济增长的渠道。实证结果表明，能源税在短期和长期内都会对实物投资产生负面影响。这一影响对公共债务的存在与否及其水平具有负向敏感性。此外，结果表明，能源税通过影响污染排放对人力资本产生间接效应。能源产品税能够减少对人力资本技能在短期和长期内产生负面影响的污染排放的流量和存量。最后，我们发现能源税在短期和长期内都可以鼓励生态创新。

Urbanization and agricultural productivity: some lessons from European cities
abstract: This article evaluates the effect of increasing urbanization on agricultural productivity at the rural-urban fringe for a set of European metropolises. It takes into account changes in total developed area, population density and the level of urban fragmentation associated with urbanization. To cope with endogeneity issues related to urban equilibrium covariates, we set up an instrumental variables strategy based on historical and institutional instruments. Our results indicate that increasing population density increases agricultural productivity at the rural-urban fringe, while increasing urban fragmentation may have a detrimental effect on agricultural productivity at low levels of fragmentation. We use instrumental variable Bayesian model averaging (IVBMA) to address model uncertainty and use an alternative panel dataset to confirm our instrumental strategy. Our results are robust to alternative model specifications and estimation methods.
abstract_zh: 本文评估了欧洲若干大都市城乡结合部中，城市化进程加快对农业生产率的影响。文章考虑了城市化过程中总开发面积、人口密度以及城市破碎化程度的变化。为应对城市均衡协变量带来的内生性问题，我们构建了一个基于历史和制度工具变量的策略。研究结果表明，人口密度的增加会提高城乡结合部的农业生产率，而城市破碎化程度的加剧在破碎化水平较低时可能对农业生产率产生不利影响。我们采用工具变量贝叶斯模型平均（IVBMA）方法来处理模型不确定性，并利用另一套面板数据确认我们的工具变量策略。研究结果对于不同的模型设定和估计方法均保持稳健。

How Does Urbanization Affect the Economy and the Environment? Policy Challenges and Research Needs
venue: International Review of Environmental and Resource Economics
abstract: Urbanization is arguably one of the most pervasive socioeconomic forces affecting economic development, ecosystem health, and human well-being. This paper analyzes the interaction between urbanization, economic development, and environmental quality and provides an overview of the literature on the interaction. We argue that the complex roles of urbanization in the economic and ecological systems necessitate a new policy approach to urbanization management. This paper also provides a brief overview of land use policies at local, regional and national levels in the European Union and the United States and discusses policy options for urbanization management. It concludes with a brief discussion of policy challenges and research needs for efficient urbanization management.
abstract_zh: 城市化可以说是影响经济发展、生态系统健康和人类福祉的最普遍的社会经济力量之一。本文分析了城市化、经济发展与环境质量之间的相互作用，并概述了该主题的相关文献。我们认为，城市化在经济与生态系统中所扮演的复杂角色，要求采用新的政策方法来管理城市化。本文还简要概述了欧盟和美国在地方、区域和国家层面的土地利用政策，并讨论了城市化管理的政策选择。最后，本文简要讨论了高效城市化管理所面临的政策挑战和研究需求。
